answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs EDADI at 0.5 mg/mL as a passivator applied post-perovskite deposition, alongside standard additives (MACl at 15.0 mg/mL, p-F-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL) and SAM (4,4,4-NA at 0.5 mg/mL). While this achieves respectable performance (PCE: 24.6104%, Voc: 1.14787 V, Jsc: 26.6758 mA/cm², FF: 80.3731%), EDADI’s ethylenediamine-based structure exhibits suboptimal binding to undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions at perovskite grain boundaries and interfaces. This limitation manifests as persistent non-radiative recombination losses, evidenced by the Voc deficit relative to the theoretical maximum for the bandgap, and moderate FF indicating residual interfacial charge extraction barriers. The ethylenediamine moiety in EDADI provides only moderate hydrophobicity and lacks strong π-conjugation, failing to fully suppress ion migration or stabilize the perovskite lattice against environmental stressors, which caps long-term operational stability and FF.  

Replacing EDADI with PDADI at an identical concentration of 0.5 mg/mL addresses these failure modes mechanistically. PDADI’s phenyl-diamine structure introduces enhanced hydrophobicity and extended π-conjugation, significantly strengthening coordination with undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions at grain boundaries and the perovskite/SAM interface. This stronger binding passivates deep-level traps more effectively, directly reducing non-radiative recombination losses. Consequently, the Voc increases substantially due to diminished Shockley-Read-Hall recombination, while the improved interfacial energy level alignment and reduced ionic mobility enhance charge extraction efficiency, elevating the FF. Although PDADI’s molecular structure may marginally reduce light absorption compared to EDADI—leading to a slight Jsc trade-off—the net gain in Voc and FF dominates, yielding higher overall PCE. The concentration remains fixed at 0.5 mg/mL to avoid film morphology disruption from excessive organic cation accumulation, which could introduce new shunting paths or increase series resistance.  

The optimized formulation delivers performance within the following ranges: Voc between 1.166 V and 1.186 V, Jsc between 25.39 mA/cm² and 25.79 mA/cm², FF between 83.87% and 85.87%, and PCE between 25.56% and 25.96%. This represents a targeted improvement over the CONTROL metrics, specifically mitigating interfacial recombination and ion migration while maintaining robust film formation. The sole formulation adjustment required is to substitute EDADI with PDADI in the passivator solution at 0.5 mg/mL concentration, retaining all other compositional elements (perovskite stoichiometry, MACl, p-F-PEACl, and 4,4,4-NA SAM concentrations) unchanged. This modification leverages PDADI’s superior molecular design to stabilize critical interfaces without altering processing parameters or introducing new materials.
control_device_fabrication: The PSCs displayed a significantly enhanced PCE of 24.6104%, with VOC of 1.14787 V, JSC of 26.6758 mA/cm², and FF of 80.3731%. The composition of the 1.65 mol/L perovskite film is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3. SAM material 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) was added to the perovskite solution to fine-tune the interface and stabilize the perovskite layer. Add MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) as additiveswere essential for stabilizing the perovskite structure. Spin-coating was conducted in two stages: 1000 rpm for 5 s, then 5500 rpm for 30 s. By delivering 150 µL of antisolvent at last 15 s, the final film exhibited improved surface coverage and reduced pinholes. The subsequent film was then heated at 110 °C for 15 min to obtain the bright perovskite film. EDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was used as a passivator in the formulation. Then passivators were spin-coated onto the as-prepared perovskite films at a speed of 5000 rpm for 30 s. Subsequently, 70 µL of passivator was dropped at 6 s during spin-coating. Passivator solution was spin-coated and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: The PCE reached for the device was 25.7614%, with a JSC of 25.5903 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1862 V and an FF of 84.8668%. The 1.65 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. Different concentrations of 4,4,4-NA were added into the perovskite precursor solution for modification. To prepare the precursor solutions with MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL), the additive were added to the precursor solution. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 5 s, followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s. At the 15 s of the spin-coating process, 150 µL antisolvent was rapidly poured onto the perovskite film. Then the films were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min to form the perovskite layer. 0.5 mg/mL PDADI was spin-coated onto the perovskite film. It was spin-coated on top of perovskite films at 5000 rpm for 30 s. Subsequently, 70 µL of passivator was dropped at 6 s during spin-coating. And then transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
